Conversely, if the system has no solutions, the proof size is exponential in the number of variables.

This conjecture tests whether algebraic closure properties inherently constrain or expand proof complexity in bounded arithmetic.

entries.statement: For any Boolean function f, the dimension of the orbit closure of the determinant polynomial under the action of the general linear group is upper bounded by the size of the smallest Boolean circuit computing f. Specifically, for a Boolean circuit C of size s, the dimension of the orbit closure of the determinant polynomial is at most O(s^2).

entries.statement: For any Max-CUT instance with n variables, the minimal eigenvalue λ_min of its degree-d SOS moment matrix satisfies λ_min ≥ Ω(1/n²). Thus, achieving a 0.879-approximation requires d = Ω(n).

entries.title: Truth-table discriminant for circuit hardness
entries.statement: There exists a poly-time-computable property P of 2^n-bit truth tables such that (i) P holds for at least 1/poly fraction of all functions, (ii) P(f) implies f requires super-polynomial circuit size over any basis.
entries.rationale: Define P via a signal-processing transform of the truth table.
entries.llm1_reasoning_excerpt: The conjecture's property P satisfies all three natural proofs criteria: (a) it is constructively computable in poly-time via the signal-processing transform, (b) it holds for 1/poly fraction of functions by design, and (c) it implies super-polynomial circuit lower bounds. This would yield an efficient distinguisher against strong PRGs, contradicting the existence of one-way functions under standard complexity assumptions.

entries.title: Stern-Brocot Rank of Truth Tables Lifts Average-to-Worst MCSP
entries.field_A: Continued-fraction / Stern-Brocot combinatorics (Hensley sums of partial quotients, Gauss–Kuzmin statistics)
entries.field_B: Average-case to worst-case hardness lifting for gap-MCSP via Yao-XOR amplification on truth-table integers

We conjecture: (i) for uniformly random f, E[SB(f)] = Θ(2^k · k) with concentration |SB − E[SB]| = O(2^k · k^{1/2}) whp; (ii) every f computed by a Boolean circuit of size s ≤ 2^{k/4} satisfies SB(f) ≤ C · s · 2^{k/2} · k for an absolute constant C; (iii) SB is XOR-additive up to slack: SB(f ⊕ g) ≥ SB(f) + SB(g) − O(k+ℓ), so any worst-case lower bound SB(h) = ω(2^{k/2}·k) on a target h amplifies via t-fold XOR into a 2^{Ω(t)} lower bound on gap-MCSP for the hardness-amplified family — a concrete avg-to-worst transfer.

The k/4 circuit-size threshold sits a polynomial factor below the Razborov–Rudich largeness threshold 2^{k/2}, so the predicted gap can in principle evade natural proofs while still yielding sub-exponential lower bounds. Continued-fraction combinatorics has essentially never been used as a circuit-lower-bound proxy, so the bridge could expose new arithmetic/structural invariants of MCSP-hard truth tables.

entries.title: Mahler Measure of Truth-Table Polynomial Lower-Bounds DNF_min
entries.field_A: Number theory of polynomial heights — the (logarithmic) Mahler measure m(p) = log|a_d| + sum_{|α|>1} log|α| over the complex roots of p ∈ Z[x] (Lehmer-Boyd-Smyth tradition: Lehmer's problem on smallest non-cyclotomic measure, Boyd's heights, Smyth's resolved cubic case). Rarely deployed in meta-complexity; computable in poly time via numerical root-finding on the explicit degree-(2^n − 1) integer polynomial.
entries.field_B: DNF_min(f): the minimum number of product terms in a DNF representation of a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} given its 2^n-bit truth table — the Hirahara–Oliveira–Santhanam restricted-MCSP proxy at the heart of meta-complexity worst-case-to-average-case reductions.
entries.statement: Define the truth-table polynomial p_f(x) := sum_{i=0}^{2^n − 1} f(i)·x^i ∈ Z[x], where f(i) is the value of f on the n-bit binary expansion of i. For every f with |f^{-1}(1)| ≥ 1, m(p_f) ≤ (DNF_min(f) − 1) · log_2(n + 1). Equivalently, every f whose truth-table polynomial has logarithmic Mahler measure exceeding (k − 1)·log_2(n+1) satisfies DNF_min(f) > k.
entries.rationale: Each DNF product term corresponds to a coordinate-aligned subcube whose index set is a coset a+W ≤ F_2^n; its indicator polynomial factors as x^a · prod_j (1 + x^{2^{i_j}}), so all roots lie on the unit circle and m = 0 (purely cyclotomic). Disjunction of k subcubes makes p_f a signed sum of k such cyclotomic-rooted polynomials, and Boyd-style sub-additive heuristics for Mahler measure under integer-coefficient sums predict at most a log_2(deg+1) escape per added term. If true, this transforms a hard Diophantine height into a poly-time-computable lower bound on DNF_min, giving a Lehmer-type obstruction useful in restricted-MCSP regimes.

entries.title: Plunnecke Doubling of Top-Fourier Spectrum Bounds ACC0 Size
entries.field_A: Additive combinatorics (Plunnecke-Ruzsa sumset doubling applied to the large-Fourier-spectrum of a Boolean function in F_2^n)
entries.field_B: ACC^0[m] circuit size for explicit Boolean functions, accessed through a Williams-style natural property R: f -> {0,1} computable in 2^O(n) time
entries.statement: Let f:{0,1}^n -> {-1,+1} with Walsh-Hadamard coefficients f_hat(a) = 2^{-n} sum_x f(x)(-1)^{a.x}, and let S(f) = {a in F_2^n : |f_hat(a)| >= 1/n} be the 1/n-large spectrum.  Define the Plunnecke doubling pi(f) = log_2 |S(f) XOR S(f)| / log_2 max(2,|S(f)|), where XOR-sumset is taken in the additive group F_2^n.  Conjecture: every f computed by an ACC^0[m] circuit of size s and depth d satisfies pi(f) <= 1 + (d log s)/sqrt(n) + o(1), and hence any explicit family with pi(f_n) >= 1.5 + Omega(1) for infinitely many n is not in ACC^0[m]; the property R := [pi >= 1.5] is constructive (computable in 2^O(n) time via FWHT) yet excludes ACC^0, threading the natural-proofs needle because R fails on sparse-spectrum PRG candidates.

Plunnecke-Ruzsa doubling of the spectrum is a Freiman-Ruzsa invariant essentially absent from the ACC^0 lower-bound literature (<5 papers cross additive-combinatorics doubling with ACC^0), giving a fresh, locally-checkable natural property aligned with Williams' algorithmic-method circuit-SAT framework.  Because pseudorandom function candidates with a designed sparse heavy-spectrum will have |S|<=2 and trivially small pi, R is not useful against PRGs, providing a concrete attempt at minimal-violation natural property.

entries.title: Monotone Ultralimit Convergence of κ along the Asymptotic Completion of the Majority Family
entries.field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW) framework / coarse geometry and Roe-algebraic K-theory within combinatorial topology
entries.field_B: Formula-depth complexity in the De Morgan basis (NC^1 vs. P lower bounds for Majority/threshold), specifically the logarithmic depth of MAJ_n and its threshold cousins
entries.statement: Let {(X_{MAJ_n}, d_{MAJ_n})} be the KW-metric spaces of the Majority family for odd n. Let c_H ∈ HX^1(X_{MAJ_n}) be the canonical Hamming cocycle c_H(x,y) = d_{MAJ_n}(x,y) mod 2, and for each propagation R let T_R ∈ C_u^*[X_{MAJ_n}] be the indicator-banded Roe operator T_R(x,y) = 1[d_{MAJ_n}(x,y) ≤ R]. Then (i) the trace-pairing-derived invariant κ_n := sup_R log|⟨c_H, T_R⟩| / log(R) is monotone non-decreasing in n, and (ii) κ_n ≥ α · log n for some absolute α > 0, so that under asymptotic_completion the limit κ_∞ = lim κ_n is unbounded. Combined with axiom A1 (Coarse-KW link), this predicts depth(MAJ_n) = Ω(log n), and combined with A5 (Roe-index rigidity) the witness is stable under coarse equivalences induced by reduction_pullback.
entries.rationale: This sub-conjecture stresses two axioms that prior sub-conjectures left untested in tandem: A1 (the Coarse-KW link, in its asymptotic, 'completion' formulation) and the convergence behavior implicit in the asymptotic_completion operation. If κ behaves like a true coarse invariant of an ultralimit, then along any natural function family it should be monotone and divergent whenever depth grows; Majority — whose formula depth is Θ(log n) — is the smallest non-trivial witness where the predicted κ-growth is detectable on tiny instances, but still nontrivial. The Hamming cocycle c_H is the simplest nontrivial coarse 1-cocycle (its δ-image is supported on triangle-defects, which vanish modulo 2 on the bipartite f^{-1}(0) ⊔ f^{-1}(1) partition), and indicator-banded T_R is the canonical Roe-controlled operator; the trace pairing reduces to a counting identity that scales with the propagation R, exactly the quantity that A1 forces to be polynomial in 2^depth. Failure of monotonicity or sub-logarithmic growth would falsify A1 in its strong form; success gives small-scale empirical evidence for the conjectured ultralimit convergence underlying A5.

entries.field_A: Leinster metric magnitude (Euler-characteristic-style invariant of finite metric spaces via inverting the similarity matrix Z(t)=exp(-t·D))
entries.field_B: Randomized communication complexity of partial Boolean matrices, with DISJOINTNESS as the canonical Ω(n) target
entries.statement: For a 2^n × 2^n {0,1}-matrix M, embed its rows as points of the Hamming metric space H(M)=({rows of M}, d_Ham) and define the magnitude τ_t(M) := 1^T Z(t)^{-1} 1 where Z(t)[i,j] = exp(-t·d_Ham(row_i, row_j)). At the canonical scale t* = ln 2 we conjecture that (a) log₂ τ_{t*}(DISJ_n) = (1 ± o(1))·n as n → ∞, and (b) every 2^n × 2^n {0,1}-matrix M satisfies log₂ τ_{t*}(M) ≤ C·R_{1/3}(M) for an absolute constant C ≤ 8; consequently τ_{t*} is a Lean-formalizable tensor invariant providing the Ω(n) lower bound on R(DISJ_n). The conjecture is falsified by exhibiting a 2^n × 2^n matrix where log₂ τ_{t*}/R_{1/3} > 8 or where DISJ_n's log₂ τ_{t*} drops below 0.5n or exceeds 1.5n for any tested n.
entries.rationale: Magnitude captures the 'effective number of distinct points' of a metric space and is monotone under inclusions of metric subspaces, so it should detect the row-diversity that any low-communication protocol must collapse via rectangular partitions. entries.field_A: Mahler measure / heights of multivariate polynomials in algebraic number theory (Smyth's L'(χ_{-3},-1) closed form for m(1+s+t); Boyd–Deninger zeta-value formulae; Lehmer's problem). entries.statement: For f:{0,1}^n × {0,1}^n → {-1,+1} with sign matrix M_f, define the multilinear matrix polynomial F_f(s_1,...,s_n,t_1,...,t_n) = Σ_{x,y∈{0,1}^n} M_f(x,y) · ∏_{i=1}^n s_i^{x_i} t_i^{y_i} ∈ Z[s,t], and its 2n-torus logarithmic Mahler measure m(F_f) = ∫_{[0,1]^{2n}} log|F_f(e^{2πiθ_1},...,e^{2πiφ_n})| dθ dφ. Conjecture: (a) m(F_{DISJ_n}) − m(F_{const}) ≥ n · m(1+s+t) − o(n) = (0.32307...)·n − o(n), and (b) for every f, R_{1/3}(f) ≥ c · (m(F_f) − n·log 2) − O(log n) for an absolute c > 0. A single instance with R_{1/3} = O(log n) but m(F_f) − n·log 2 = ω(log n) refutes (b); an instance of DISJ with sublinear m refutes (a).
entries.rationale: The multilinear polynomial F_f is the natural Fourier-side / generating-function avatar of M_f under the {0,1}^n × {0,1}^n product structure; for DISJ the polynomial factors as 2∏(1+s_i+t_i) − ∏(1+s_i)(1+t_i), whose Mahler measure inherits Smyth's exact L-value per coordinate and gives a clean Ω(n) signature, while easy functions (constant, equality up to a row/column permutation, low-rank patterns) collapse F_f into a product of small-height factors with bounded m. Heights/Mahler measure are coordinate-respectful (multiplicative under tensor product, monotone under specialization), so they should track the multiplicative structure that makes DISJ hard, in a way orthogonal to spectral or discrepancy invariants.

entries.title: Lasserre Moment-Rank Gap of Accept Set Bounds AC0 PARITY Size
entries.field_A: Sum-of-squares / Lasserre hierarchy moment-matrix theory (Lasserre 2001, Parrilo 2003, Grigoriev 2001) — specifically the empirical degree-k pseudo-moment Gram matrix M_k(f) := (1/|f^{-1}(1)|) sum_{x in f^{-1}(1)} v_k(x) v_k(x)^T over the multilinear monomial vector v_k(x) of degree <= k on the boolean cube, used here as an S_n-equivariant non-uniform circuit invariant rather than as a CSP relaxation; its R-rank is poly-time via SVD and is essentially absent from the AC^0 / switching-lemma literature.
entries.field_B: AC^0 depth-d formula size for PARITY_n in the Hastad / Razborov-Smolensky lineage; the canonical NEXP-vs-AC^0 gateway target where tight size constants for d>=3 remain open.
entries.statement: For every boolean f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1} and integer k <= n/2, let rk_k(f) := rank_R(M_k(f)) <= N_k where N_k = sum_{j<=k} C(n,j). Conjecture (A): rk_k(PARITY_n) = N_k for every k <= floor(n/2) (full Lasserre rank of the even-parity accept set up to half-degree). Conjecture (B): for every AC^0 depth-d formula F of size s computing g on n variables, rk_k(g) <= s * k * C(n, k-1) for every 2 <= k <= n/2. Combining (A) and (B) at k = ceil(n^{1/(d-1)}) forces any AC^0 depth-d formula for PARITY_n to have size >= N_k / (k * C(n,k-1)) = 2^{Omega(n^{1/(d-1)} / log n)}; one counterexample to (A) at any (n,k <= n/2) or to (B) at any (F,k,g) refutes the conjecture.
entries.rationale: PARITY's accept set is the unique S_n-invariant antipodal half-cube and so should saturate every Lasserre moment-matrix dimension below half-degree, while AC^0 formulas of size s decompose their accept set as a union of s subcubes whose moment-matrix support sits inside an O(s)-dimensional (k*C(n,k-1))-spanned subspace of the multilinear monomial basis (one degree-(k-1) factor per gate fan-in). Re-expressing the Hastad/Razborov barrier as a moment-matrix rank deficit makes the lower bound a single linear-algebraic invariant computable in O((2^n + N_k) N_k^2) time. The bridge sits squarely in the SOS-hierarchy framework — Lasserre level-k rank for empirical pseudo-distributions on f^{-1}(1) — while being a non-uniform circuit lower bound rather than a CSP integrality gap, occupying a corner with <5 papers.

entries.title: Schur-Horn Majorization Gap Lower-Bounds Sign-Rank Discrepancy
entries.field_A: Schur-Horn majorization theory (doubly-stochastic / diagonal-vs-spectrum majorization on Hermitian matrices)
entries.field_B: Discrepancy-based randomized communication complexity of ±1 sign matrices
entries.statement: For any ±1 matrix M of size N×N (N=2^n), let s(M)=(s_1≥…≥s_N) be its singular values and d(M) be the sorted absolute row-sums of M divided by sqrt(N); define the Schur-Horn majorization gap G(M)=sum_{k=1}^{N} (s_k - d_k)_+ /N. Then the discrepancy disc(M) satisfies disc(M) ≤ C · 2^{-G(M)} for an absolute constant C∈[1,4], and equivalently the randomized two-party communication complexity obeys R_{1/3}(M) ≥ G(M) - O(1). The conjecture is falsified by exhibiting any single ±1 matrix with disc(M) > 4·2^{-G(M)} at any tested n≤6.
entries.rationale: Schur-Horn theory precisely measures how far a Hermitian matrix's diagonal can be from its spectrum under unitary conjugation, which is exactly the kind of unitary-invariant slack that controls cut-norm/discrepancy via Grothendieck-type inequalities. Because Hadamard-like matrices saturate the spectrum-vs-diagonal majorization inequality, G(M) should track the spectral flatness that Lindsey's lemma exploits, giving a fresh majorization handle on discrepancy that is independent of the algebrization barrier. No prior work links Schur-Horn majorization gaps directly to sign-rank or randomized communication complexity.

entries.title: Median-Restriction Hardness Amplification Gap for DNF Truth Tables
entries.field_A: Quantile statistics of random subcube restrictions (order-statistic / median-of-medians combinatorics on the Boolean cube; rarely deployed in worst-case-to-average-case amplification, distinct from Hastad/Razborov switching-lemma expectation-style bounds)
entries.field_B: DNF-MCSP / minimum DNF term count DNF_min(f) for a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} given its 2^n-bit truth table — the Hirahara–Oliveira–Santhanam restricted-MCSP proxy used in average-to-worst-case meta-complexity reductions
entries.statement: Let M_p(f) be the median, over 1024 i.i.d. random p-restrictions ρ (each variable independently *-ed with probability p, else uniform 0/1) with p = 1/sqrt(n), of the term count DNF_min(f|_ρ) of the restricted truth table; let A_p(f) be the corresponding mean. We conjecture that for every Boolean function f on n ≤ 16 variables, DNF_min(f) ≤ 2 · M_p(f)^2 + n, and moreover the median–mean gap satisfies A_p(f) − M_p(f) ≤ sqrt(DNF_min(f)) · log2(n+2). One Boolean function violating either inequality refutes the conjecture.
entries.rationale: Switching-lemma arguments bound *expected* restricted-DNF size, but average-to-worst-case lifts (Impagliazzo–Wigderson, Hirahara) actually need a tail/quantile statement: a typical restriction must already reveal hardness, not just the expectation. Replacing the mean by the median controls heavy-tailed restriction outliers and conjecturally yields a sharper, square-rooted relation to the unrestricted term count, exposing the structure that lets average DNF-MCSP hardness amplify to worst-case via restriction self-reducibility. The bridge is rare because order statistics of restriction-size functionals (as opposed to expectations) have not, to my knowledge, been used as a complexity invariant.

entries.title: Diameter-Multiplicity Power Law under Controlled Refinement Recovers Coarse Depth
entries.field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW); coarse geometry / Roe-style coarse cohomology of finite KW metric spaces (Gromov asymptotic dimension, Roe algebras)
entries.field_B: Formula-depth complexity (NC^1 vs. P): obtaining super-logarithmic formula-depth lower bounds for explicit f by reading off the multiplicity exponent of a controlled cover of X_f
entries.statement: Let f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1} be explicit and let X_f be its KW-metric space with metric d_f. For any sequence of controlled covers U_0, U_1, U_2, ... of X_f produced by iterated controlled_refinement, with diameters R_k = R_0 · 2^{-k} and multiplicities m_k, the conjecture is that the asymptotic exponent γ(f) := limsup_{k→∞} log(m_k) / log(R_0/R_k) satisfies γ(f) = κ(f) up to additive O(1). Equivalently: the slope of log(m_k) versus log(R_0/R_k) recovers the coarse depth invariant from the framework's target, and hence by axiom A1 lower-bounds depth(f). In particular for an explicit family with γ(f_n) = ω(log n), one obtains depth(f_n) = ω(log n).
entries.rationale: This sub-conjecture directly tests the proof mechanism asserted by axiom A1, which states that the multiplicity exponent of a controlled cover equals depth (the cover is built from a KW protocol tree, and refinement halves diameter at the cost of one extra fan-out at each gate, so multiplicity should compound at the depth rate). It also exercises the controlled_refinement operation as a numerical probe rather than a structural one, providing an alternative empirical handle on κ(f) that bypasses construction of explicit cocycles in HX^1. If A1's proof is correct, the diameter–multiplicity log-log slope must match κ(f) on independently checkable small instances; deviation would signal a gap in A1's translation step. It is independent of the previously listed conjectures because it concerns the refinement operation rather than the trace pairing, the ultralimit, oracle collapse, pullbacks, or composition.
entries.llm1_reasoning_excerpt: The proposed invariant γ(f) is read off the truth table of f via a constructive procedure (build X_f, greedy/ILP cover, fit log-log slope) running in time poly(2^n), so it is constructive in the Razborov–Rudich sense. The target class is formula depth ω(log n), i.e., super-NC^1, which sits inside P/poly, so usefulness against P/poly-style classes is at stake. entries.title: Diagonalization separation of P and NP
entries.statement: By Turing-machine diagonalization, there exists L in NP minus P.
entries.rationale: Diagonalize against all poly-time TMs.
entries.llm1_reasoning_excerpt: The proof sketch relies on diagonalization against all polynomial-time Turing machines, a black-box simulation technique that treats machines solely by their input-output behavior. Such methods are known to relativize, as they do not exploit structural properties of computations like circuit depth or formula locality. entries.llm2_reasoning_excerpt: The proposed proof uses Turing-machine diagonalization against all poly-time TMs, treating them as black boxes, which is a relativizing argument. This approach does not exploit specific properties of the circuit or formula encoding, triggering the relativization barrier. As established by Baker-Gill-Solovay, such arguments cannot separate P from NP due to the existence of oracles A and B with P^A = NP^A and P^B ≠ NP^B.
